title: EPTS: Elastic Post-Training Sparsity for Efficient Large Language Model Compression

problem.claim: Large language models need compression for efficient deployment on resource-constrained devices.

gap.claim: Existing post-training sparsity methods typically optimize one sparsity level at a time, requiring separate re-optimization for each deployment requirement.

contributions.claim: EPTS is a unified multi-sparsity framework that produces one elastic model for diverse sparsity configurations through one-shot optimization.
MS-HiLoRA enables knowledge inheritance from lower- to higher-sparsity groups to mitigate competition for parameter reconstruction.
MSFM dynamically fuses feature representations at different sparsity granularities to improve adaptability to pruning perturbations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on LLaMA and OPT families reportedly show competitive performance against SparseGPT and Wanda, with efficiency gains from single-optimization multi-scenario deployment.

narrative_sequence.summary: Post-training sparsity is positioned as important for compressing language models for constrained-device deployment.
Single-sparsity optimization makes adaptation to different sparsity requirements costly and inflexible.
EPTS addresses the problem with one elastic model trained across multiple sparsity configurations in one optimization.
MS-HiLoRA supports cross-sparsity knowledge inheritance, while MSFM mixes representations across sparsity granularities.
The authors report competitive results and efficiency gains on LLaMA and OPT families.

source_observation.claim: A single model is designed to support multiple sparsity configurations through one-shot optimization.

interpretation.claim: Sharing optimization across deployment configurations may reduce repeated adaptation cost.

application.claim: For deployment environments with varying hardware sparsity requirements, consider jointly optimizing a model for multiple configurations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach remains effective for sparsity configurations, models, or hardware settings beyond those evaluated.

unknowns: Exact sparsity configurations, datasets, evaluation metrics, baselines, and quantitative results are not provided.
Optimization cost, inference overhead, memory requirements, and implementation details are not provided.
The abstract does not specify the limits of robustness across hardware scenarios or pruning perturbations.
